sections.text: Yellow perch anglers experienced a slight resurgence over the past week. Anglers fishing east of Sterling State Park toward the Ohio state line in 24 feet of water caught decent-sized yellow perch on minnows. Multiple limits were not reported for multi-person boats. Water temperatures continued to drop, helping improve activity. A few walleye were caught in the same area on nightcrawler harnesses, though catches were scattered. Smallmouth bass fishing on Lake Erie was good using various artificial lures.
Fishing pressure was low over the past week. A few yellow perch were caught east of the Spark Plug in 20 feet of water, with morning hours being most productive.

When weather permitted, boat anglers caught immature Chinook salmon and steelhead in 50 to110 feet of water. Orange and green spoons fished in the top 50 feet of water worked best. Anglers casting from the breakwalls were unsuccessful targeting mature Chinook salmon.

Decent numbers of immature Chinook salmon and steelhead were caught in 60 to 150 feet of water. Orange, green, and yellow spoons worked best when targeting the top 60 feet of water. Pier anglers targeting Chinook salmon were unsuccessful.

Boat anglers caught good numbers of fish. Anglers targeted fish in approximately 100 feet of water. Pier fishing slowed, though an occasional salmon was still caught. Casting spoons was the most productive method. Overall fishing was very slow, and no yellow perch were reported.

Boat anglers caught a few fish, with the most productive water located around 80 feet of water. Fishing was slow overall, but that remained the most effective depth. Pier fishing was very slow for all species. Yellow perch fishing continued to produce good results. Fish remained scattered, with 40 to 60 feet of water proving to be the most productive range.
Decent numbers of salmon were caught in the lower river as well as at the Berrien Springs dam.
Coho salmon and Chinook salmon were caught in the Tawas River. A few yellow perch were caught off Standish. Otherwise, fishing effort was light.

Very little boat activity was observed over the past week. Anglers who targeted deeper water reported catching lake trout, steelhead, Atlantic salmon, and an occasional walleye. Standard-sized spoons trolled in 30 to 50 feet of water yielded inconsistent success. No fishing activity was reported on the pier.

Anglers reported a slow bite. Spinners, small crankbaits, and drifted beads yielded some success for coho salmon and Atlantic salmon. Chinook salmon turned dark, but anglers continued to catch fish on spoons and spawn. A few steelhead were taken on drifted beads and small spawn bags.
Boat anglers reported a few steelhead and immature Chinook salmon while trolling in 40 to 80 feet of water. With cold water temperatures, the best results came in the top 25 feet of the water column.

There was a mixture of silver and dark Chinook salmon at the Cheboygan Dam spillway. Anglers who floated or bottom-bounced spawn were the most successful, landing up to three salmon. Spoons and minnow-style crankbaits were productive as well.

Anglers targeting salmon off the pier experienced a slow week, with a few Chinook salmon and coho salmon caught. Glow spoons and body baits such as bandits, flicker shads, and Rapala J-13s were popular choices. Anglers targeting channel catfish off the pier with nightcrawlers and cut bait had decent success.

Anglers casting Rapala J-13s, flicker shads, and Jr. ThunderSticks in black/silver and fire tiger colors caught a few Chinook salmon. Glow spoons and skein were also successful. A few steelhead and coho salmon were caught on spinners.

Pier fishing was slow. Anglers fishing straight out and south caught a limited number of Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and steelhead in 150 to 200 feet of water at various depths. Fish were caught from 20 to over 100 feet down on plugs and spoons.

Anglers fishing the Bear River reported slow fishing for Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and steelhead. Anglers had success using spawn and skein in the Bobber Hole early in the morning. Those casting from piers reported occasional bites using spoons.

Anglers launching at the Center Road boat launch caught a few cisco along with a few Chinook salmon when trolling in 110 to 140 feet of water. Anglers who had success trolled a mix of spoons and plugs roughly 60 to 80 feet down. A few smallmouth bass were also caught along the breaks in 25 to 45 feet of water.

Anglers targeted steelhead off the piers as water temperatures cooled, though action was slow. Coho salmon and Chinook salmon remained in the area as they slowly moved toward river mouths. The Betsie River continued to hold good numbers of Chinook salmon in deep holes and near Homestead Dam. Boat anglers caught a few Chinook salmon and coho salmon in front of the piers early in the morning on spoons. As morning conditions cleared, anglers moved out to the shelf to target steelhead in the top 30 feet of water.

Anglers targeting yellow perch reported scattered schools and had difficulty locating fish. Some anglers reported catching yellow perch in shallow water using worms. Walleye anglers reported slow fishing, though fishing overall was good. Drifting or trolling crawler harnesses worked well. Anglers also reported having success using jigheads tipped with nightcrawlers or leeches. Coho salmon anglers reported slow fishing and fewer fish sightings. Anglers fishing the Escanaba River had success.

Over the past week, the river experienced very light angling effort. Rough weather conditions throughout the week hindered fishing conditions on occasion. Catches of walleye were reported in very low numbers.

The Ontonagon, Silver City, and Union Bay access sites all experienced light angling effort over the past week. Heavy winds and frequent rain showers limited lake access on multiple days. Anglers reported catches of lake trout, coho salmon, Chinook salmon, and brown trout in low to fair numbers. Fish were caught by anglers trolling in depths ranging from 30 to 150 feet of water.

Angling effort from the harbor was light over the past week. Inclement weather limited lake access. When weather permitted, anglers reported mixed catches of brown trout, steelhead, coho salmon, and lake trout in low numbers. These fish were caught by anglers trolling in depths of 30 to 150 feet of water.

Overcast conditions made for good fishing, with anglers catching fish throughout the day. Most anglers caught at least one fish, while a few others landed up to 10 fish. Floating or bottom-bouncing skein produced the best results. Salmon were actively moving in and out of Nunns Creek, while a fresh push at the Carp River provided anglers with an opportunity to hook into a silver Chinook salmon at the Carp River cement footing pier. Salmon were caught throughout the stretch between McDonald Rapids and the Carp River cement footing pier. Other productive bait options included spoons, minnow-style crankbaits, and spinners. Glow baits were effective before daybreak and after sunset.
Shore anglers caught coho salmon and rainbow trout at the mouth of the Sucker River. Fishing with spawn and casting spoons brought success. Boat anglers did well jigging for lake trout.

Anglers reported Chinook salmon and pink salmon in the river. Anglers reported having the most success using skein, though some anglers had success using spinners and shallow-diving crankbaits. Orange, chartreuse, and pink were popular lure colors. The best success occurred at night and early in the morning.

Anglers caught lake trout in 80 to 160 feet of water. Most anglers continued to troll north of White Rocks out toward Granite Rock and the Clay Banks, as reports west of the Chocolay River yielded poor results. Anglers reported catching lake trout throughout the water column, primarily near the bottom using downriggers. A few reports indicated anglers caught lake trout and coho salmon off the lower breakwall early in the morning and near sunset. Anglers trolling the river mouths near Lower Harbor caught decent numbers of coho salmon and Chinook salmon. Brown trout and coho salmon were caught in both the Chocolay River and Carp River. Fish numbers increased with cooler evening temperatures.

The tribal nets were removed, opening the Flats northwest of Au Train Island toward Five Mile Point for lake trout fishing. The Wood Island Reef and areas northwest of Au Train Island out toward the Laughing Whitefish River also remained available for lake trout fishing, while Au Train Bay to the Laughing Whitefish River was open for salmon, brown trout, and steelhead. Anglers jigging near Au Train Island in 40 to 80 feet of water had good success catching lean lake trout. All lake trout caught were near the bottom while trolling or jigging. Anglers targeting brown trout and salmon in 10 to 60 feet of water marked numerous fish.

Anglers reported fair to good fishing, with catches consisting primarily of coho salmon and splake while trolling near river mouths, along with a few brown trout. Shore anglers reported that the bite picked up, with many anglers successfully catching coho salmon and splake. Anglers jigging for lake trout and lake whitefish reported a slow bite.

Anglers reported fair fishing for lake trout when trolling spoons and flasher/fly rigs around structure in 50 to 100 feet of water. Anglers reported a few coho salmon, but in very low numbers. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported a fair bite when using natural presentations, with most fish caught in 80 to 120 feet of water.

Anglers in Hessel caught a few yellow perch near the buoy straight out from the Cedarville boat launch. A few northern pike were caught off the pier in Hessel. Smallmouth bass anglers had good success fishing around island rock piles and points. Splake fishing was slow due to 66-degree water temperatures within the marina. Splake season is now closed. In DeTour, anglers caught good numbers of lake trout prior to the season closing. Lake trout season is now closed, and fishing pressure in DeTour was minimal.

Boat anglers caught approximately 30 good-sized yellow perch per vessel over the weekend in Michigan waters, potentially marking the start of their seasonal return. Anglers fished east of Stony Point near the Ohio border using minnows on perch rigs. Water temperatures continued to drop, which should improve conditions. Virtually no walleye were caught over the past week as fish remained in deeper water. Largemouth bass were active along submerged cover.
Yellow perch and walleye fishing was poor due to northeast winds, with only a few yellow perch and walleye caught in the lower Saginaw River.

High winds kept fishing effort to a minimum in many areas. A few yellow perch were caught in the slot off Fish Point, though numbers were low. Anglers fished half-day trips to keep five to eight fish, with extensive sorting required. Northern pike were also caught by anglers casting various artificial lures in the Quanicassee River. Elsewhere, fishing activity and effort remained slow.

Overall fishing was slow. Pier anglers tried fishing off the rocky south pier at the boat launch without success. A few boat anglers caught yellow perch inside the harbor using bobbers and minnows. The north pier remained inaccessible, and the boat launch continued to operate with only one working dock.

Silver fish began to appear nearshore, with a few anglers reporting coho salmon and steelhead off the north and south breakwalls. Spoons, spinners, and spawn were effective, though the movement of salmon and trout remained relatively slow. Some anglers caught northern pike and smallmouth bass off the south breakwall using spinners. Boat fishing remained slow, with few fish caught. Access along the inside of the north breakwall was limited due to dredging.

Anglers caught coho salmon off the pier. A few anglers had success using spoons and spinners when targeting coho salmon, with many caught along the inside wall of the harbor. Water conditions were murky but showed signs of clearing. Windy conditions limited boat angling activity while pier anglers benefited.

Boat anglers reported fair salmon action 25 to 80 feet down in 70 to 140 feet of water. Spoons in green, blue, and orange worked well. The south breakwall in Muskegon is closed due to lighthouse repairs.

Boat anglers found immature Chinook salmon, steelhead, and a few lake trout 30 to 80 feet down in 60 to 180 feet of water. Spoons were most productive in green and orange. Pier anglers reported slow salmon action, though a few mature salmon were caught using glow spoons, alewives, and gizzard shad. The north pier in Grand Haven is closed, with a projected reopening in the summer of 2028.

Pier fishing was slow for all species, with only an occasional Chinook salmon or steelhead caught. Boat anglers had good success targeting salmon in around 60 feet of water using plugs and spoons. No perch reports were received.

Fishing pressure remained high on the piers, though fishing was slow for all species. A handful of salmon and steelhead were caught by anglers casting spoons or crankbaits. Boat anglers continued to catch a few fish around the pierheads, with better fishing reported in around 60 feet of water using spoons. Perch fishing was fair, with fish scattered in 40 to 60 feet of water.
Salmon fishing was slow in the lower river. Salmon were present in the area, but fishing was difficult. Some salmon caught near the Berrien Springs Dam.
Salmon fishing slowed in the river. A few fish were still caught while trolling, though action was overall slow.

Wind kept most boat anglers off the water. The anglers who were able to fish reported slow fishing when targeting walleye and yellow perch. Coho salmon and Chinook salmon were caught in the Tawas River on spawn and various artificial baits.

Boat anglers targeting 40 to 60 feet of water had some success on lake trout, along with a few Atlantic salmon and coho salmon. Fish were still well scattered throughout the water column. A few walleye were also caught using standard-sized spoons on leadcore and downriggers. Anglers reported slow Chinook salmon action, with only a few fish caught.

While anglers reported seeing both coho salmon and Chinook salmon, the catch rate was low. Anglers who found success drifted spawn and beads. Casting glow spoons produced a few fish after dark. A few Atlantic salmon were caught while casting spinners and drifting beads.

Anglers targeting lake trout had success in 55 to 100 feet of water on spoons, flashers, and Spin-N-Glos. With cold water moving in, the majority of fish were caught in the top 40 feet of water. A few salmon were caught in the same depth on medium-sized spoons. Walleye anglers reported slow fishing, with only a few fish caught. Pier anglers had no success.

Anglers at the Cheboygan Dam spillway caught low numbers of Chinook salmon, along with an occasional coho salmon, pink salmon, or steelhead. A handful of Chinook salmon were caught at the Cheboygan pier. Salmon and trout were caught when casting small spoons or minnow-style crankbaits, as well as drifted or bottom-bounced beads and spawn. Small walleye, smallmouth bass, and rock bass were also caught between the Cheboygan Dam and State Street drawbridge while drifting nightcrawlers.

Boat anglers trolling spoons early in the morning caught a few coho salmon and Atlantic salmon off the pierhead in 15 to 30 feet of water. A few Chinook salmon were also caught on spoons and J-plugs. Anglers casting from the pier found similar success, catching a few coho salmon and Chinook salmon while casting spoons, spinners, and body baits early in the morning. Blue and silver, orange, and green were popular spoon colors, while fire-tiger and clown were effective patterns for body baits such as Bandits or J-13s. Anglers casting body baits or jigheads with split-tail plastics off the pier caught walleye at dusk.

Anglers targeting coho salmon and Chinook salmon in the harbor found limited success while casting spoons, spinners, and Jr. thundersticks. A few salmon were caught this week along with a steelhead, with dawn and dusk being the most productive times.

Adult Chinook salmon were present in 20 to 30 feet of water off Swan Bay. Anglers trolled plugs and Bombers off planar boards. Lake trout and immature Chinook salmon, along with the occasional steelhead, coho salmon, and walleye, were caught outside of the bay or straight out from the harbor. Lines were set throughout the water column near baitfish. Spoons were the most effective choice, with standard-sized and slim-profile models performing best. Effective lure colors included white, green, blue, orange, yellow, and glow patterns during early morning and late evening hours.

Anglers were sparse due to rough and windy weather conditions. When boat anglers were able to get out, lake trout were caught off Stoneport and between the lighthouses. An occasional Chinook salmon was caught off Stoneport, False Presque Isle, and off the Grand River outlet north of the marina. Steelhead, coho salmon, and walleye were caught incidentally. The most productive depths ranged from 45 to 80 feet of water, with lines set throughout the water column. Anglers trolled a mix of J-Plugs and spoons. Effective lure colors included white, green, blue, orange, and glow patterns during early morning and late evening hours.

Anglers targeting salmon reported slow fishing. A few fish were caught just outside the pierheads and in Manistee Lake by boat anglers trolling plugs and jigging spoons. Pier fishing was fair for anglers targeting Chinook salmon and coho salmon while casting spoons. Anglers fishing along the shelf reported a few Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and steelhead in the top 40 feet of water in 150 to 200 feet of water. Fish were caught using spoons and plugs in glow, purple, and orange colors.

Pier fishing was very slow, though a few salmon were caught during late night hours. Boat anglers trolling for chinook salmon caught a limited number in the channel, in the harbor, and straight out in 50 to 80 feet of water. Salmon and a few steelhead were also caught to the northwest in 60 to 80 feet of water, as well as in 60 to 140 feet of water at and around Big Sauble Point in the top 40 feet of water using spoons and plugs. Steelhead were caught on orange colors.

Water temperatures cooled significantly over the past week, with the temperature break holding near 35 feet down. Boat anglers trolling reported inconsistent salmon catches throughout the week. Chinook salmon were found 40 to 80 feet down in more than 80 feet of water, while an occasional coho salmon was caught in the upper 40 feet. Anglers targeting fish near Medusa Creek reported slow but steady action early in the morning while drifting skein or casting and trolling body baits.

Boat anglers targeting salmon reported slow action near the end of the Petoskey breakwall while trolling in roughly 30 feet of water. Anglers casting spoons and body baits off the pier and Clock Dock reported steady results. Anglers targeting salmon in the Bear River reported catches on flies and skein. An occasional steelhead was caught while drifting the river and trolling from boats.

Anglers heading south of the Center Road launch caught lake trout along with a few Chinook salmon when trolling in 80 to 140 feet of water. A mix of plugs and spoons worked well. A few cisco were caught around Old Mission roughly 50 to 70 feet down in 90 to 120 feet of water.

Lake trout along with a few Chinook salmon were caught by boat anglers trolling in 120 to 150 feet of water along the west bank just north of Elmwood Marina. A mix of spoons and flasher-fly combinations worked well. Boat anglers trolling near the Red 6 Buoy in 100 to 120 feet of water caught a few lake trout. Anglers caught salmon while trolling in 100 to 125 feet of water near the mouth of the Boardman River.

Anglers targeted Chinook salmon on the First Bank in 100 to 300 feet of water. Water temperature was reported to be 42 degrees from the surface down to 100 feet of water. Fishing was sporadic with no thermocline present. Anglers targeted all portions of the water column, catching coho salmon and Chinook salmon in 30 to 60 feet of water on blue and orange trolling spoons. Lake trout fishing was productive in 100 to 120 feet of water using attractors such as cowbells fished directly on the bottom. Pier anglers had the best success catching Chinook salmon before sunrise while drifting skein.

Cooler water moved into the area along with Chinook salmon and coho salmon. Chinook salmon continued to move into the Betsie River in lower numbers, with anglers reporting good action in deeper holes. Pier anglers casting spoons and rigging alewives reported very good fishing during late evening and early morning hours. Boat anglers trolling offshore in the early morning and evening reported good numbers of 2-year-old Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and an occasional steelhead.
Anglers trolling the channel and just out front of the light house reported a few coho salmon caught on spoons in the early morning hours.
Boat anglers targeted yellow perch throughout Suttons Bay, Omena Bay, and Northport, though few anglers reported success when using natural bait.

Anglers targeting coho salmon fished the Escanaba River. Anglers reported seeing fish surface in the river and near the dam. Fishing was slow, with most anglers unable to entice bites. Anglers drifted spawn and cast brightly colored lures. Anglers noted that the run was slowing down, though additional heavy rainfall could bring in remaining coho salmon. Walleye anglers reported fair fishing, with success using natural bait trolled on a harness or cast on a jighead, as well as artificial lures such as snap jigs and crankbaits.

Boat anglers caught a few coho salmon while trolling in the bay. Lake trout anglers had success jigging and trolling around Grand Island and Wood Island. Anglers fishing off the mouth of the Anna River caught a few splake and coho salmon. Casting spinners and drifting spawn produced the best results.
Angling effort on the river was very low over the past week. Recent reports indicated occasional catches of walleye in low numbers. Early morning hours were the most productive.

Angling effort from Ontonagon increased over the past week, with effort from the Silver City and Union Bay access sites increasing significantly. Anglers reported mixed catches of lake trout, brown trout, coho salmon, and Chinook salmon in fair numbers. Boat anglers trolling found fish in depths ranging from 30 to 150 feet. Anglers had better success finding salmon when trolling in shallower water.

Angling effort from the harbor increased slightly over the past week. Anglers reported catches of brown trout, coho salmon, Chinook salmon, and lake trout, with lake trout and coho salmon being the most frequently reported. Fish were caught by boat anglers trolling in 30 to 160 feet of water. Anglers had better success targeting salmon when trolling in shallower water.

Anglers reported salmon moving into Nunns Creek and closer to McDonalds Rapids in the Carp River. Anglers casting spoons and drifting spawn from shore at Nunns Creek caught few Chinook salmon. At the Carp River, Chinook salmon and pink salmon were caught using spoons, spinnerbaits, crankbaits, beads, and spawn.

Boat anglers had success targeting lake trout when trolling and jigging. A few coho salmon were caught by boat anglers trolling east of the breakwall. Shore anglers also caught a few coho salmon near the mouth of the Sucker River while casting spoons.

Pink salmon were plentiful in the river. Anglers targeting pink salmon used small crankbaits, spinners, and beads, typically in pink colors. Chinook salmon anglers reported catching fish in holes of fast water above the U.S. Highway 2 bridge. Anglers reported the best success on skein, though other egg patterns also produced fish. Anglers trolling the river reported slow salmon fishing but caught incidental species such as smallmouth bass and northern pike.

Anglers targeted lake trout in 80 to 160 feet of water. Most boat anglers continued to troll north of White Rocks out toward Granite Rock and the Clay Banks, as reports from west of the Chocolay River remained dismal. Anglers reported catching lake trout throughout the water column, though most fish were caught near the bottom using downriggers. A few anglers caught lake trout and coho salmon off the lower breakwall early in the morning and before sunset. Anglers trolling the river mouths out of Lower Harbor caught fair numbers of salmon, including both coho salmon and chinook salmon. Brown trout were among the most frequently caught species in both the Chocolay and Carp rivers, along with numerous coho salmon. Following rain and cooler temperatures, fish numbers began to increase as salmon pods staged near the river mouths ahead of the run.

Tribal nets were reset in the flats northwest of Au Train Island toward Five-Mile Point, requiring caution when navigating that area. Wood Island Reef and the waters northwest of Au Train Island toward the Laughing Whitefish River remained open for lake trout fishing, while Au Train Bay to the Laughing Whitefish River remained open for salmon, brown trout, and steelhead. Anglers jigging near the bottom in 40 to 80 feet of water in front of Au Train Island had good success catching lean lake trout. All lake trout taken this week were caught near the bottom while trolling or jigging. Anglers targeting brown trout and salmon in shallow water marked numerous fish, though few catches were reported. As angler effort increases over the coming weeks, activity is expected to pick up, particularly off river mouths, Scott Falls, and the Laughing Whitefish River area.

Anglers reported fair to good fishing with catches consisting primarily of coho salmon, lake trout, and a few splake while trolling. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported fair action using natural and artificial presentations in 100 to 140 feet of water. Shore anglers reported improved fishing over the past week, with many anglers catching coho salmon.
Fishing activity remained slow, with most anglers targeting walleye and yellow perch. Anglers had the best success jigging in 10 to 15 feet of water using natural bait.

Anglers reported fair to good lake trout fishing while trolling spoons and flasher-fly rigs around structure in 50 to 100 feet of water. Anglers reported a few coho salmon and steelhead were caught while trolling, but in very low numbers. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported fair fishing using natural presentations, with most fish caught in 80 to 120 feet of water.

Anglers caught yellow perch in Cedarville within Cedarville Bay and Government Bay. Anglers also caught good numbers of larger smallmouth bass around rocky structures near the islands in Hessel. Splake fishing was extremely slow due to warm weather and elevated water temperatures delaying fish movement. In DeTour, anglers targeted walleye with little success but caught yellow perch near Drummond Island. Anglers also caught good numbers of lake trout while trolling the flats prior to the end of the season on Sept. 30.

I’m looking forward to some cooler temps, migratory fish, and all of the other activities that the fall season brings. We are capping off the summer season mousing… There’s still a week or two left…

Unfortunately the weather did not really cooperate and it made for a tough couple of days of fishing. Early in the week we had some cloudy weather which made for a good iso bite…

The flooding and worm flow events shuffled the deck and gorged the fish. I spent a significant amount of time searching water for rising fish…

Most of our rivers have just returned to normal levels or slightly higher than normal depending on where you are at. There is rain in the forecast so I would expect…
